This second part examines that gesture in detail through quantum mechanics—unitarity, many worlds, decoherence, and quantum biology—arguing four main propositions: observer neutrality, a strict timescale constraint in neural tissue, the distinction between fine-grained information conservation and pattern continuation ("conserved but not continued"), and the failure of quantum immortality as a survival guarantee. items.title: MERLIN SCIENCE — Documentary Index Lacks Mathematical Content for Analysis — E8 Intelligence Research
items.summary: The finding is simple, and it is this: a documentary index, no matter how well curated, contains no mathematical content that can be analyzed. The titles and abstracts are bibliographic metadata, not primary research. From that metadata alone, I can derive no equations, no constants, no ratios, and no geometric relationships. The depth of mathematical information present is exactly one on a scale of ten. That is not a failure of the search; it is a structural property of the source material. items.title: Computational and Equivariant Extensions of Riemannian Geometry for Geometric World Models: Volume III — Discrete Approximations, Stochastic Dynamics, and Geometric Priors
items.summary: This third volume continues the series by addressing the computational realisation of Riemannian structures on latent manifolds and their integration with equivariant architectures and stochastic dynamics. It treats discrete differential geometry on graphs and meshes, numerical approximations of the Levi-Civita connection and curvature, Riemannian Langevin dynamics and stochastic gradient flows, and the systematic incorporation of geometric priors through equivariant neural networks and geometric deep learning. The discussion emphasises practical consequences for the design, training, and analysis of geometric world models, including JEPA-style predictors and spatial intelligence systems.

items.title: Neuromorphic Event-Camera Imaging and Image Reconstruction
items.summary: Event cameras, also known as dynamic vision sensors, depart from the synchronous frame-based imaging paradigm by reporting per-pixel brightness changes asynchronously as a stream of events. Each event encodes a pixel coordinate, a microsecond-resolution timestamp, and the polarity of a logarithmic-intensity change that has crossed a contrast threshold. This principle yields microsecond temporal resolution, a dynamic range exceeding $120$~dB, sparse output, and very low power, making event cameras attractive for high-speed and high-dynamic-range scenarios in which conventional cameras suffer from motion blur and saturation. items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) seeks to turn gains in an AI system into a stronger capacity to produce subsequent gains.
